name: Nigeria
tagline: The loudest country on the continent
summary: One in five Africans is Nigerian. Afrobeats, Nollywood, the Benin bronzes, Yankari's elephants and the Obudu plateau — a country that exports its culture faster than anywhere else on earth.
when: Dry season across the country, and the festival calendar sits inside it.

entries.caption: The Loudest Country on the Continent
entries.description: Two hundred and twenty million people, and the music and film the rest of the continent watches.
entries.subject: the Lagos skyline across the lagoon at dusk

entries.caption: Mangrove to Sahel
entries.description: Niger delta mangrove in the south, rainforest, savanna, and the Sahel at the Niger border.
entries.subject: mangrove creeks in the Niger delta

entries.caption: Yankari and Gashaka
entries.description: Yankari's elephant herds, and Gashaka-Gumti's forest chimpanzees on the Cameroon border.
entries.subject: elephants at the Wikki warm spring in Yankari

entries.caption: Yankari
entries.description: The country's best game reserve, with a warm spring you can swim in at the centre of it.
entries.subject: a game track through Yankari savanna at first light

entries.caption: The Obudu Plateau
entries.description: Sixteen hundred metres of grassland on the Cameroon border, with cattle ranches and cloud.
entries.subject: the green Obudu plateau under low cloud

entries.caption: Erin-Ijesha and Gurara
entries.description: Erin-Ijesha's seven stages in Osun, and the Gurara falls on the road to Abuja.
entries.subject: the stepped Erin-Ijesha waterfall in forest

entries.caption: The Niger and the Benue
entries.description: Two great rivers meeting at Lokoja, and the delta they build a thousand kilometres downstream.
entries.subject: the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers at Lokoja

entries.caption: Lagos and the Atlantic
entries.description: Tarkwa Bay, Elegushi and the long Atlantic beaches east towards Lekki.
entries.subject: boats and beach umbrellas at Tarkwa Bay, Lagos

entries.caption: Cross River
entries.description: The Cross River forest holds the last of Nigeria's gorillas and some of West Africa's tallest trees.
entries.subject: dense rainforest canopy in Cross River state

entries.caption: Plateau and Delta
entries.description: Hiking the Jos plateau, the Obudu cable car, and creek trips through the delta.
entries.subject: the rock formations of the Jos plateau

entries.caption: Five Hundred Languages
entries.description: Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa and around five hundred more, in one country.
entries.subject: a Yoruba drumming group performing at a festival

entries.caption: Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Fulani
entries.description: Four large cultures and hundreds of smaller ones, each with its own courts and calendars.
entries.subject: a Fulani herder with cattle in northern Nigeria

entries.caption: Jollof, Suya and Egusi
entries.description: Suya off the grill at night, egusi with pounded yam, and the jollof question again.
entries.subject: suya being grilled at a roadside stand at night

entries.caption: Osun-Osogbo and Calabar
entries.description: The Osun-Osogbo grove festival in August, and the Calabar carnival through December.
entries.subject: dancers in costume at the Calabar carnival

entries.caption: Bronze, Adire and Aso Oke
entries.description: Benin bronze casting still practised in Igun street, and adire resist-dyed cloth in Abeokuta.
entries.subject: a bronze caster at work in Igun street, Benin City

entries.caption: Benin City and Sungbo's Eredo
entries.description: The walls of Benin, and Sungbo's Eredo — a hundred and sixty kilometres of earthworks.
entries.subject: the earth walls and moat of the Benin kingdom

entries.caption: The Bronzes
entries.description: The Benin bronzes are the reason half the museums of Europe have a Nigeria problem.
entries.subject: a display of Benin bronze plaques

entries.caption: Lagos, Abuja, Kano
entries.description: Lagos on the lagoon, purpose-built Abuja in the middle, and Kano's thousand-year-old walls.
entries.subject: the old city and dye pits of Kano

entries.caption: Mud Mosques and Modernism
entries.description: Hausa mud architecture in the north, and the 1970s modernism of Lagos and Abuja.
entries.subject: the Hausa mud architecture of a northern emir's palace

entries.caption: Danfo and Buka
entries.description: The yellow buses, the roadside buka, and a city that does not stop at any hour.
entries.subject: a yellow danfo bus in Lagos traffic

entries.caption: Loud, and Welcoming
entries.description: Not a quiet holiday — but there is nowhere friendlier once you are through the door.
entries.subject: children playing football on a Lagos beach

entries.caption: Hike, Paddle, Ride
entries.description: The Jos plateau, the Obudu ranch trails, and creek boats through the delta.
entries.subject: hikers on a trail across the Obudu plateau

entries.caption: Lagos Island Hotels
entries.description: Victoria Island and Ikoyi at one end, and Obudu's mountain resort at the other.
entries.subject: a hotel terrace overlooking Lagos lagoon at night

entries.caption: Community Forest
entries.description: Afi Mountain's drill ranch and the Cross River community forests, both village-run.
entries.subject: drills at the Afi Mountain sanctuary in Cross River

entries.caption: Colour and Crowd
entries.description: Markets, festivals and cloth — the hardest thing here is choosing what to leave out.
entries.subject: a crowded cloth market in southern Nigeria

entries.caption: Idanre
entries.description: The Idanre hills, with an old town six hundred steps up and nobody else climbing them.
entries.subject: the granite Idanre hills rising above forest

entries.caption: The Culture Everyone Else Is Watching
entries.description: Afrobeats and Nollywood came from here, and it is worth seeing where.
entries.subject: a live Afrobeats performance in Lagos
